chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi and al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, all from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the time for Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers, so he said: 'When the sun departs (from its zenith), the time for both Dhuhr and 'Asr enters, but this one [Dhuhr] is before this one ['Asr]. Then you are in the time for both of them together until the sun sets.'

key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Departure of the sun from its zenith

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the shared temporal window for Dhuhr and 'Asr, establishing that while Dhuhr is preferred earlier, both prayers remain valid from solar zenith until sunset. This supports the Shia practice of *Jam'* (combining prayers) by demonstrating their contiguous validity, a principle rooted in the Quranic command to 'establish prayer at the decline of the sun' (17:78).
